RESULT: P=43, D=12, H=31, H with delta!=0 = 28. SUM(delta) = -1.0320 h; the exact value is -1.032033 = -61922/60000, plus about 4e-15 of float noise. In per_mandate, n counts the P entries (D and H together). Sum of the negative deltas: -2.7987; positive: +1.7667. Three H rows have delta=0: JAN!27 (12.3-13.3), MAY!44 (11.45-12.45), MAY!45 (12.45-13.45). This matches the earlier "-1,03 h on 43 entries, 12 forcément décimales".

How it was run: DB copied to /tmp/tb-g4-1405/a03-a/staging-copy.db (sha 958c76ed..., the same as /tmp/tb-g4-0842/staging-now.db) and opened with mode=ro. Workbooks copied to src-orig/ and src-r1/, sha checked, and parsed with a stdlib XML reader (openpyxl is not installed). All scripts were run with python3 -I. QUIRKS:
(1) raw_json holds str() of the openpyxl value, so every value is a JSON string ("11.45", "9"), never a JSON number. The only way to know a value is a number is to parse it. Cell types were checked against the workbook XML: all 86 start/end cells of the 43 P lines are numeric cells (t=n, format 0.00), and none is a text cell. raw_json matches the source workbook for all 2247 linked lines.
(2) SEPT 26!82 (entry 1358, NHAF 2026, active) has start=12.2513, with 4 decimals. The importer flagged it clock_rounded and stored 12:15; declared hours are 0.7487. Under the definition this line is in P/H with frac=round(25.13)=25, giving delta -0.1654. If it is read as 12.25, or rebuilt from the stored HH:MM 12:15, it drops out of P: P=42, H=30, 27 nonzero, sum -0.8667, active sum -0.4667. That reproduces the earlier "-0,87 h".
(3) Truncating frac with float int() instead of round(): 12.2 gives 19 and 15.6 gives 59, so SEPT 26!53/54 move from D to H. Result: D=10, H=33, 30 nonzero, sum -1.0820.
(4) The "-1,67 h on 42 entries" figure was not reproduced by any variant I tested. Variants tried: float truncation; D rows computed in h.mm with or without the +24 rule (+71.0 / -1.83 / -2.00); 12.2513 read as 12.25; rebuilding from stored HH:MM; reading the whole workbook.
(5) Declared hours are Excel formulas (=end-start on decimal numbers): 2240 of the 2247 hours cells are formulas. So raw_json and entries.hours carry float noise, e.g. 0.8000000000000007 on 39 of the 43 P lines. Rows above show stored_hours rounded to 4 decimals. For all 43 P lines, declared = decimal clock difference within 1e-6, so no P line has declared != clock. The only linked line flagged declared_vs_clock_mismatch is JUN!13 (entry 2187: 9-12 with 4 h declared). Its clocks are integers, so it is outside P.
(6) R1 vs original: 42 entries come from R1 (batches 0ba463.../00bf396..., sha a6f6b7..., which is /tmp/tb-g4-0842/A/corr.xlsx). R1 differs from the original only in 33 date cells in column B. Start, end and hours are identical, and none of the 43 P lines comes from R1, so the choice of source does not change the figure.
(7) Entries corrected after import: none in this DB copy. entry_changes is empty, the audit log has no entry update events, entries.hours equals the raw declared hours for all 2247 entries, and the stored start/end equal the decimal reading for all 43 P lines. This contradicts the brief, which says some entries were corrected after import.
(8) AVR!32 and JUN!31 (entries 194 and 421) have date-formatted clock cells. raw_json holds '1900-01-13T12:00:00' (importer flag clock_from_date_format), so they are excluded as non-numbers. Their underlying serials (13.5/15.5 and 11.5/13) are multiples of 0.25, so they would be outside P anyway. 6 linked lines have empty start/end, which also keeps them out of P.
(9) The +24 midnight rule never applies to any H row.
(10) Workbook line JUL 26!39 (NHAF, 8.5 to 8.45, declared -0.05) was never imported (decision excluded_project/error). A computation that reads the workbook instead of the DB would put it in H, and the +24 rule would add +23.97 h.
(11) Each entry is linked to exactly one ledger row with entry_id (2247/2247; 11 COMMITTED batches). The same sheet!row appears in up to 11 batches with entry_id NULL, so joining on sheet/row instead of entry_id multiplies rows.

calcul_b.quirks:
The figure is -1.0320 h (exactly -1.03203...). It was computed twice, independently, and both runs agree: (a) from the workbook cells (openpyxl data_only=True plus formulas, plus a direct read of the raw XML <v> values), mapped to entries through import_batch_rows (source_sheet, source_row), with each batch tied to its file by file_sha256; (b) from raw_json in the database alone. The earlier '-1.03 h on 43 entries, 12 forcément décimales' figure was correct.

Breakdown:
- Active mandates (projects.active=1): 14 entries in P. NHAF 2026 has 7 (2 D, 5 H, all 5 with delta != 0, sum -0.2320). STC GEM Oct - DM job has 7 (1 D, 6 H, all 6 nonzero, sum -0.4000). PCR LV 2026, EUROPCR 2027 and MSD have none.
- Three H rows have delta = 0 because start and end have the same fraction: JAN!27 (12.3 to 13.3), MAY!44 (11.45 to 12.45) and MAY!45 (12.45 to 13.45).
- D rows (delta = 0 by definition): MAY!69, AUG!163, MAR 26!99, MAR 26!100, MAY 26!18, JUN 26!62, JUN 26!95, SEPT 26!53, FEB 26!24, JUL 26!48, FEB 26!23, SEPT 26!54.
- No H row crosses midnight.

Quirks that could make another computation differ:

1) SEPT 26!82 (entry 1358, NHAF 2026, active). It is the only value with more than 2 decimals: start = 12.2513 (XML 12.251300000000001). The cell format is 0.00, so Excel displays 12.25. The importer flagged it clock_rounded and stored start 12:15, with stored hours 0.7487 (the formula end minus start). Under the spec, frac = 25, so it is H with delta -0.1654. If the raw values are rounded to 2 decimals before the 0.25 test, it drops out of P: |P| = 42, sum = -0.8667, active sum = -0.4667. This exactly explains the earlier '-0.87 h' figure.

2) The earlier '-1.67 h on 42' figure could not be reproduced. Variants tried:
- truncating frac instead of rounding: -1.0820, and 2 D rows become H (16.6 or 15.6 stored as ...0.59999 truncates to 59);
- truncation plus 2-decimal rounding: -0.9167;
- also computing D rows in h.mm: -0.9987, or -0.8333 with 42 rows;
- rounding stored hours to 2 decimals: -1.0333.

3) raw_json stores str(value), so it cannot tell a text cell '11.45' from a number 11.45. The workbook shows no text start/end cells and no formulas in start/end for any of the 2247 entries. Six entries have empty clocks: JUN!6, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12. Two have date-typed cells (Excel 1900 serials, h:mm format; raw_json '1900-01-13T12:00:00' etc.): AVR!32 = 13.5 to 15.5 and JUN!31 = 11.5 to 13.0. They are multiples of 0.25, so they stay outside P whether or not they are read as numbers. All 43 hours cells in P are end-minus-start formulas whose cached values equal the stored hours.

4) Some XML values carry binary noise (18.149999999999999, 16.600000000000001). Use the shortest repr or round; truncating the frac misclassifies them.

5) Stored hours carry float noise (0.8000000000000007 etc.). Every nonzero delta is at least 0.033 h, so any tolerance from 1e-9 to 0.01 gives 28.

6) R1 (corr.xlsx, a6f6b7ef) differs from the original only in 33 date cells of column B. No start, end or hours cell differs. All 43 P rows come from batches of the original file (c93c610c). The two R1 batches (42 entries) contribute none.

7) No corrections after import exist in this copy:
- entry_changes is empty and there are no entry_* audit events;
- entries.hours equals the cell value for all 2247 entries;
- every numeric pair's start_time/end_time equals the decimal reading.
ckpt.db and A/snap.db are identical for the 43 rows. A/premandats.db has the same entries but all 24 projects active, so an 'active' figure computed on it would be -1.0320 over 43.

8) Declared hours differ from the decimal clock only at JUN!13 (entry 2187: 9 to 12, declared 4 h), which is outside P. Inside P, declared hours equal the decimal duration. Entry 1358's stored clock 12:15 to 13:00 (0.75) is 0.0013 h off its stored 0.7487.

9) No value lands on a half hundredth, so Python's half-even round versus half-up changes nothing.
